subject: Hosted API Uplift onramp — rate matrix proposal & execution steps
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@horizonlabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling Horizon usage — proposing a monthly commit uplift

Hi Tessa,

We've been really happy with the latency and cost profile since migrating more routes to Redwood's hosted API. Q1 consumption exceeded our forecast by ~35% (see attached breakdown), and we want to lock in predictable capacity for the next 12 months.

Specifically, we'd like to discuss:
- Increasing our monthly committed tokens from our current tier to a 40% uplift
- Preferential rate bands for token usage beyond the commit (to avoid large overage surprises)
- A phased billing cadence for the first 3 months so we can align forecasting with our finance team

Can you put together a short proposal with suggested tiers, incremental per-token rates, and any operational changes we'd need to enable (burst pockets, soft throttle window, regional pinning)? Marcus (cc'd) and our procurement team will review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon Labs
attachments: horizon_q1_usage_breakdown.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@horizonlabs.com>, Marcus Cole <marcus@horizonlabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling Horizon usage — proposing a monthly commit uplift

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the usage file, that helps.

We can absolutely put together a leaning proposal that balances predictability and unit economics. High level next steps:
1) I'll draft a two-option proposal (Conservative: +25% commit with tighter overage rate; Aggressive: +50% commit with stepped rate breaks)
2) Ops/Capacity will validate burst ability for regional pinning and confirm soft throttle thresholds (Vanessa looped in)
3) We'll provide a 90-day phased billing cadence option and a DocuSign-ready amendment for whichever option you select

Do you prefer a short call tomorrow (30 mins) to walk the options, or should we send the draft first?

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Horizon's ask. Quick checklist:
- Capacity: can we support a staggered +40% commit for their west-region workloads without impacting existing SLOs? (They want regional pinning to us-west and mixed burst to us-east only on overflow)
- Pricing: propose two options (Conservative +25% commit, Aggressive +50% commit) with accompanying overage rates and 90-day phased billing for the first quarter
- Legal/billing: any constraints on invoice cadence for a phased ramp? They asked for a 90-day smoothing option.

I've attached their usage file. Can you reply with a concrete rate matrix and operational caveats by EOD tomorrow? I'm aiming to send a customer-facing proposal Friday.

Thanks,
—Tessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2029 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaling Horizon usage — proposing a monthly commit uplift

Tessa / Vanessa — reviewed their Q1 numbers. Summary and proposal below.

Operational notes:
- We can accommodate a +40% committed token uplift pinned to us-west with no degradation to current SLOs, provided they accept a 5% soft-throttle window during sustained burst periods (>90th percentile for 12 hours). We recommend enabling prefix KV caching on the most common endpoints to reduce marginal tokens by ~8-12%.
- Burst fallback to us-east will be available but subject to cross-region egress penalties (call this out to the customer).

Pricing matrix (proposed):
Option A — Conservative - Monthly commit: +25% - Committed unit rate: $0.0009/token - Overage band 1 (0–20% over commit): $0.0012/token - Overage band 2 (>20%): $0.0016/token - 90-day phased billing: invoices split 60/30/10 for the first three months (customer requested smoothing)

Option B — Aggressive - Monthly commit: +50% - Committed unit rate: $0.00082/token (volume discount) - Overage band 1 (0–25%): $0.0011/token - Overage band 2 (>25%): $0.00145/token - 90-day phased billing: invoices 50/30/20

Notes for sales language: call out KV cache recommendation and the soft-throttle caveat. Also prepare a short appendix on expected monthly spend delta and projected token burn for 6 months (I can generate numbers if you want).

—Karthik
Director, Capacity & Performance, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@horizonlabs.com>, Marcus Cole <marcus@horizonlabs.com>, procurement@horizonlabs.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API uplift proposal & next steps (DocuSign link)

Hi Sarah / Marcus — thanks for the conversation last week. Per our discussion, attached is a concise proposal with two options and the operational caveats Karthik highlighted.

Executive summary:
- We recommend Option B (Aggressive) if Horizon needs predictable headroom for upcoming feature launches; it offers a lower committed unit rate and smoother overage bands.
- If finance prefers lower upfront commitment we can adopt Option A with tighter overage protection.
- Both options include: regional pinning to us-west, KV caching recommendations, and a soft-throttle policy (5% window) during sustained spikes.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached amendment and select Option A or B.
2) If approved, sign the attached DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/secure/DocID=5a7f2c
3) Once signed we will: schedule an ops-runbook handoff, apply regional pinning, and enable the phased billing cadence for the first 90 days.

I've copied Karthik and Vanessa for the operational handoff. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
